title: Validate an Untrusted Command Frame
statement:
A device receives command frames from a network it does not trust. Before anything acts on one, a validator must check it. The validator has to be **safe on any bytes at all**: it must never read outside the frame it was given.

## The frame

```
type  paylen  payload (paylen bytes)  counter (4 bytes, big-endian)
 0      1      2 .. 2+paylen-1         2+paylen .. 5+paylen
```

Total length is exactly `2 + paylen + 4`.

## The policy (an allow-list)

| `type` | Name | `paylen` | Payload | Allowed range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x01` | SET_POWER | 2 | signed 16-bit, big-endian | `-7000 .. 7000` |
| `0x02` | SET_MODE | 1 | unsigned 8-bit | `0 .. 3` |
| `0x03` | SET_LIMIT | 2 | unsigned 16-bit, big-endian | `0 .. 10000` |

Any other `type` is **not allowed**.

## Your function

```
int validate_command(const uint8_t *frame, size_t len, uint32_t *last_counter);
```

Run the checks **in this order**. Return the first code that applies.

| Order | Check | Return |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `len < 6`, or `len != 2 + paylen + 4` | `-1` |
| 2 | `type` is not in the table | `-2` |
| 3 | `paylen` is not the one the table gives for this `type` | `-3` |
| 4 | the payload value is outside its range | `-4` |
| 5 | `counter <= *last_counter` (a replay) | `-5` |
| | all good | `0` |

On success, and **only** on success, set `*last_counter` to this frame's counter. A rejected frame must not change it. The first counter ever accepted must be at least 1, because the harness starts `*last_counter` at `0`.

The harness feeds one frame per line, in hex, to the **same** `last_counter`, and prints one return code per line.

## Watch out

- You may read `frame[1]` only after you know `len >= 6`. You may read the payload only after the length check.
- Never trust `paylen` to be consistent with `len`. Check it first.
- SET_POWER is **signed**. `0xFFFF` is `-1`, which is in range.
- A replay is rejected even when everything else is valid.

tests.name: power just out of range
tests.description: Rejected frames leave the counter alone, so counter 1 and 2 are both still fresh.
